articleTitle: Quaternionic Algebra Described by Sp(1) Representations
abstract: This paper shows that representations of the unit quaternion group Sp(1) can be used to describe the most important spaces in quaternionic algebra. Sp(1) representations are found to underlie both the AH‐modules of Joyce and the sheaf‐theoretic approach to quaternionic algebra given by Quillen, giving a clearer understanding of the link between these two theories. Sp(1) representations are used to derive the algebraic structure of stable AH‐modules and their quaternionic tensor products, enabling us to obtain the algebraic structures of quaternion holomorphic functions on R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Framed Discs Operads and Batalin–Vilkovisky Algebras
abstract: The framed n‐discs operad fD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is studied as semidirect product of SO(n) and the little n‐discs operad. Our equivariant recognition principle says that a grouplike space acted on by fD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is equivalent to the n‐fold loop space on an SO(n)‐space. Examples of fD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>‐spaces are nerves of ribbon braided monoidal categories. We compute the rational homology of fD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, which produces higher Batalin–Vilkovisky algebra structures for n even. We study quadratic duality for semidirect product operads and compute the double loop space homology of a manifold as BV‐algebra.

articleTitle: A Torelli Theorem for the Moduli Space of Higgs Bundles on a Curve
abstract: Let X be a smooth projective curve over C, and let M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>,<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ξ</sup> be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles on X (with genus g > 1), of rank n and fixed determinant ξ, with n and deg(ξ) coprime. Let X′ and ξ′ be another such curve and line bundle. We prove that if M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>,<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ξ</sup> and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X′</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>,<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ξ′</sup> are isomorphic as algebraic varieties, then X and X′ are isomorphic.

articleTitle: A Non‐Associative Rickart's Dense‐Range‐Homomorphism Theorem
abstract: The aim of this paper is to discuss the non‐associative side of a celebrated theorem of C. E. Rickart asserting the automatic continuity of dense range homomorphisms from complete normed associative algebras to complete normed strongly semisimple associative algebras. As the main result, we prove that associativity can be removed in Rickart's theorem whenever the range algebra is Jordan‐admissible.

articleTitle: The Paucity Problem for Certain Pairs of Diagonal Equations
Subgroups of M‐Groups
abstract: A bordered Klein surface, or real algebraic curve with real points, of algebraic genus p ≥ 2 admits at most 12(p − 1) automorphisms. Automorphism groups which attain this bound are called M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐groups. Given a bordered Klein surface X of genus p which admits 6(p − 1) or 3(p − 1) automorphisms, we study whether the full automorphism group of X has the maximum number 12(p − 1) of automorphisms. This leads to a characterization of all M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐groups which contain normal subgroups of index two or four. This characterization cannot be extended to M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐groups with normal subgroups of other indices. In addition, our results provide a new method for constructing infinite families of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐groups, and we illustrate this with several examples.

articleTitle: Characterization of Mixing in Quotients of R‐Trees
abstract: If T is an R‐tree and Γ is a group of isometries acting properly discontinuously on T, it is shown that the geodesic flow on the quotient metric space X = T/Γ, when restricted to the non‐wandering set, is topologically mixing if and only if the lengths of the closed geodesics in X generate a dense subset of R.

articleTitle: Strong Subdifferentiability of the Norm on J B‐Triples
abstract: We prove that the norm of a J B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triple X is strongly subdifferentiable at a norm‐one element x if and only if 1 is an isolated point of the triple spectrum of x, and this is the case if and only if the support of x in the bidual of X lies in X. Moreover we show that the J B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triples whose norms are strongly subdifferentiable at every point of their unit spheres are precisely the weakly compact J B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triples. Characterizations of those norm‐one elements of a J B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐ or J B W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triple where the norm is Fréchet differentiable are also obtained.

articleTitle: On Maximal Abelian Subalgebras of Real Factors
abstract: We will show the real algebra version of S. Popa's theorem, which answered Kadison's problem about maximal abelian subalgebras. As applications, some results about involutory <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐antiautomorphisms are obtained.

articleTitle: Morita Equivalence for C*‐Algebras with the Dunford–Pettis Property and C‐Crossed Products
abstract: Let unital C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebras A and B be Morita equivalent and let X be an A–B‐imprimitivity bimodule. Then it is shown that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) A has the Dunford–Pettis property; (2) B has the Dunford–Pettis property; (3) X has the Dunford–Pettis property. Furthermore, we discuss when C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐crossed products by actions or coactions have the Dunford–Pettis property.

articleTitle: On Cantor Sets in 3‐Manifolds and Branched Coverings
abstract: It is known that any Cantor set C in a 3‐manifold M (open or closed) is tamely embedded in the boundary of a k‐cell Δ, for k = 2, 3 (R. P. Osborne, 1969). It is proved that there exist a k‐cell Δ and a 3‐fold branched covering of M over (a subset of) S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> such that (i) C is tamely embedded in the boundary of Δ, (ii) Δ projects homeomorphically onto a k‐cell Δ̂ tamely embedded in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and (iii) C is sent onto a tame Cantor set T tamely embedded in the boundary of Δ̂. The argument uses techniques of branched coverings and is independent of Osborne's theorem.

articleTitle: The Tits Construction and the Exceptional Simple Classical Lie Superalgebras
abstract: We construct the exceptional simple classical Lie superalgebras D(2, 1; α) (α ≠ 0, −1), G(3), and F(4) by means of the Tits construction.

articleTitle: Linear Statistics of Low‐Lying Zeros of L‐Functions
abstract: We consider linear statistics of the scaled zeros of Dirichlet L‐functions, and show that the first few moments converge to the Gaussian moments. The number of Gaussian moments depends on the particular statistic considered. The same phenomenon is found in random matrix theory, where we consider linear statistics of scaled eigenphases for matrices in the unitary group. In that case the higher moments are no longer Gaussian. We conjecture that this also happens for Dirichlet L‐functions.

articleTitle: Weierstrass Points of Genus‐2 Surfaces with Regular Fundamental Domains
abstract: Let X be a genus‐2 surface with a regular fundamental domain. The six Weierstrass points of X are determined here in a purely geometric way, as intersection points of certain simple closed geodesics.

articleTitle: Applications of Summing Inclusion Maps to Interpolation of Operators
abstract: We study interpolation of operators between abstract real method spaces by using thin Banach ideal properties of the inclusion maps between Banach sequence spaces generating these spaces. An application to interpolation of operators on scales of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>‐spaces is presented.

articleTitle: Numerical‐Radius‐Attaining Polynomials
abstract: In this paper we discuss a version of James theorem making use of polynomials which attain their numerical radius. In addition, we obtain a characterization of finite‐dimensional Banach spaces in terms of such polynomials.

articleTitle: A Note on the Distribution of Rational Points on Threefolds
abstract: Let T ⊂ P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> be a non‐singular threefold of degree at least four. Then we show that the number of points in T (Q), with height at most B, is o(B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) or B → ∞.

articleTitle: Exact, Continuous Boundary Crossings Out of Convex Sets in RN
abstract: The existence of the unique point at which a line segment crosses out of a located convex set in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> is proved constructively, and the continuity of the resulting mapping is investigated.

articleTitle: Rational Complete Intersections
abstract: As a generalization of a paper of Hirschfeld and Thas in Contemporary Mathematics 111, we consider the following problem. If S is a subset of the GF(q)‐rational points of an elliptic curve C, determine a curve D such that S = C ∩ D.

articleTitle: Lipschitz Homogeneous Banach Spaces
abstract: Define a Lipschitz homogeneous space to be a Banach space Lipschitz equivalent to all its closed subspaces. It is proved that a Lipschitz homogeneous Banach space with the Radon–Nikodym property must be isomorphic to l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: The Kernel of the Equivariant Kirwan Map and the Residue Formula
abstract: Using the notion of equivariant Kirwan map, as defined by R. F. Goldin [3], we prove that—in the case of Hamiltonian torus actions with isolated fixed points—the Tolman and Weitsman description of the kernel of the Kirwan map can be deduced directly from the residue theorem of L. C. Jeffrey and F. C. Kirwan [6, 7]. A characterization of the kernel of the Kirwan map in terms of residues of one variable (that is, associated with Hamiltonian circle actions) is obtained.

articleTitle: On Lagrange's Theorem with Prime Variables
abstract: It is conjectured that Lagrange's theorem on four squares is true for prime variables, that is, every large integer n with n ≡ 4 (mod 24) is the sum of four squares of primes. In this paper, the size for the exceptional set in the above conjecture is reduced to O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/5+ε</sup>). The new ingredients include an iterative method to treat the enlarged major arcs, and a hybrid estimate for Dirichlet polynomials.

articleTitle: Stepanov's Method Applied to Binomial Exponential Sums
abstract: For a prime p and binomial ax<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> + bx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</sup> with 1 ≤ l < k < 1/32(p – 1)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup>, we use Stepanov's method to obtain the bound |Σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p−1</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x=1</inf>e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(ax<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> + bx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</sup>)| ≪ max {1, lΔ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/3</sup>}<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/4</sup> k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/4</sup> p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/4</sup>, where Δ = (k – l)/(k, l, p – 1).

articleTitle: Subrings in Quadratic Fields Which are Not Universal for GE2
abstract: Let F be a quadratic field and let S be a finite set of places containing S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>, the set of infinite places in F. Let v be a finite place outside S, S′ = S ∪ {v}, R = O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf>, and R′ = O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S′</inf>. In this paper, some examples are given to show that if the prime ideal P in R corresponding to v is non‐principal or the natural homomorphism R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> → (R/P)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> is not surjective then, although R is universal for GE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, R′ may not be universal for GE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Restricted Weak Type Inequalities for Convolution Maximal Operators in Weighted LP Spaces
abstract: Let φ : R → [0, ∞) be an integrable function such that φχ(−∞, 0) = 0 and φ is decreasing in (0, ∞). Let τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>f(x) = f(x – h), with h ∈ R\{0} and φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>(x) = (1/R)φ(x/R), with R > 0. In this paper we study the pair of weights (u, v) such that the operators M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τhφ</inf>f(x) = sup<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R>0</inf> |f| * [τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>φ]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>(x) are of restricted weak type (p, p) with respect to (u, v), 1 ≤ p < ∞. As particular cases, these operators include some maximal operators related to Cesàro convergence. We characterize those functions φ for which M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τhφ</inf> is of (restricted) weak type (p, p) with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Unlike the case of the Cesàro maximal operators, it follows from the characterization that the interval of those p such that M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τhφ</inf> is of weak type (p, p) can be left‐closed, [p0, ∞], or left‐open, (p0, ∞], without having restricted weak type (p0, p0).

articleTitle: Conjectures on Character Degrees for the Simple Lyons Group
abstract: We prove a version of the Isaacs–Navarro conjecture for the simple Lyons group. The original conjecture is a refinement of the Alperin–McKay conjecture which deals with irreducible characters of height zero and the normalizer of a defect group. But we look also at the normalizers of radical p‐chains and consider the alternating sum of the numbers of characters of any given defect.

articleTitle: Counting Rational Points on Diagonal Quadratic Surfaces
abstract: For any ε > 0 and any diagonal quadratic form Q ∈ Z[x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>] with a square‐free discriminant of modulus Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</inf> ≠ 0, we establish the uniform estimate ≪εB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2+ε</sup> + B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+ε</sup>/Δ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/6</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</inf> for the number of rational points of height at most B lying in the projective surface Q = 0.

articleTitle: Weighted Ergodic Theory And Dimension Free Estimates
abstract: Let T = {T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∈R</inf> be a strongly continuous one‐parameter group of positive operators acting on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(μ), where μ is a σ‐finite measure and 1 ≤ p < ∞. We develop a weighted ergodic theory associated with T which parallels the classical theory of A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>‐weights. A weighted transference principle is obtained in this setting and used to establish dimension free weighted inequalities for certain classical operators, including the higher‐order Riesz transforms.

articleTitle: Symplectic Bifurcations of Plane Curves and Isotropic Liftings
abstract: We study the classification of varieties in the Marsden–Weinstein reduction and their liftability. In particular the complete symplectic classification of the Bruce–Gaffney plane curve singularites is provided and is applied to obtain naturally the Lagrangian openings.

articleTitle: Relative Hitchin–Kobayashi Correspondences for Principal Pairs
abstract: A principal pair consists of a holomorphic principal G‐bundle together with a holomorphic section of an associated Kaehler fibration. Such objects support natural gauge theoretic equations coming from a moment map condition, and also admit a notion of stability based on Geometric Invariant Theory. The Hitchin–Kobayashi correspondence for principal pairs identifies stability as the condition for the existence of solutions to the equations. In this paper we generalize these features in a way which allows the full gauge group of the principal bundle to be replaced by certain proper subgroups. Such a generalization is needed in order to use principal pairs as a general framework for describing augmented holomorphic bundles. We illustrate our results with applications to well‐known examples.

articleTitle: Generalized Calabi–Yau Manifolds
abstract: A geometrical structure on even‐dimensional manifolds is defined which generalizes the notion of a Calabi–Yau manifold and also a symplectic manifold. Such structures are of either odd or even type and can be transformed by the action both of diffeomorphisms and closed 2‐forms. In the special case of six dimensions we characterize them as critical points of a natural variational problem on closed forms, and prove that a local moduli space is provided by an open set in either the odd or even cohomology.

articleTitle: Transversally Harmonic Maps between Manifolds with Riemannian Foliations
abstract: We consider leaf preserving maps between manifolds equipped with Riemannian foliations. We construct a transversal tension field for such maps. Then we introduce the notion of transversally harmonic maps. In the last section of the paper we present some examples of transversally harmonic maps.
